title: Dominic and the Atlas
premise: In 1899, Wren Brightwater, an apprentice clockmaker raised in a workshop of orphans and strays by the enigmatic Dominic Vale, is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock. There she discovers a sealed letter revealing that Dominic's household was assembled to guard an inheritance — a patent and a fortune that a powerful shipping family will stop at nothing to claim before the century turns. As sabotage, betrayal, and old debts close in, Wren learns each member of her found family has a claim on what remains, but only one berth exists: passage and protection for a single heir. In the end, Wren refuses the choice as it was written, forging a new document that divides the inheritance among them all — and claims her own place not as heir, but as the one who keeps time for everyone.
about_author: Yara Underhill is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Victorian horological ledgers before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the North Sea coast, where she repairs antique clocks that no longer keep perfect time.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Wren Brightwater, POV. In the cramped Brightwater workshop, Wren finishes her apprenticeship piece while the other members of Dominic's household — cook, clerk, retired sailor — drift through their evening rituals. She measures her life in small, portable things. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by the sense that belonging here is borrowed.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Black Wax
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. A courier delivers a sealed summons from the Royal Observatory requesting the master clockmaker; Dominic is too ill to travel, so Wren must go alone. That night she glimpses Dominic burning correspondence, one envelope bearing black wax. Emotional beat: first crack in her trust, mixed with pride at being chosen.

chapters.title: The Observatory at the Edge of the City
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Arriving at the hilltop observatory, Wren meets Keeper Aldous Finch, who treats her with odd deference, as if he expected someone else. The master clock is sabotaged, not broken — a gear deliberately misfiled. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Dominic Kept
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Repairing the clock, Wren finds hidden inside its case a letter naming 'the Brightwater household' as custodians of the Vale inheritance — patents, shares, and a deed — and warning of the Harrow Shipping Company's claim. Emotional beat: vertigo; her family is a plot she never agreed to.

chapters.title: The Household at Supper
chapters.summary: Marisol the cook, POV. Back home, Marisol observes the household's fragile rituals as a stranger from Harrow's firm comes asking questions. Each member deflects differently, revealing how much they each know. Emotional beat: protective love laced with fear that the family is built on secrets.

chapters.title: Finch's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Keeper Finch admits he served Dominic thirty years ago and helped hide the inheritance documents inside the clock, trusting no vault. He warns Wren that when the century turns, the trust expires and the estate passes to whoever holds the letter. Emotional beat: dread of responsibility landing on the youngest shoulders.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Workshop
chapters.summary: Tobias the clerk, POV. The workshop is ransacked; Dominic's ledgers are stolen, and Dominic collapses searching for them. Tobias, who came to the household fleeing debt, suspects his past has caught up with him. Emotional beat: guilt and the terror of losing the only home he's known.

chapters.title: The Harrow Offer
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Edmund Harrow himself visits, offering Wren a partnership and legitimacy if she surrenders the letter. He speaks of family as blood and name — everything hers is not. She refuses, but his parting words about Dominic's true history unsettle her. Emotional beat: temptation braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Old Salt's Map
chapters.summary: Ezra the retired sailor, POV. Ezra reveals he once crewed for Dominic and knows the inheritance includes more than paper: a ship, the Atlas, moored and forgotten in the estuary. He draws a map from memory. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against the temptation to finally claim something of his own.

chapters.title: Dominic Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Recovered enough to talk, Dominic confesses he gathered orphans and strays deliberately — heirs of circumstance, bound by choice rather than blood — and that the letter names all of them, but the law recognizes only one signature. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude colliding; the family was always real, but never safe.

chapters.title: The Stolen Ledger Returns
chapters.summary: Marisol, POV. The ledger reappears on the doorstep, pages torn out — left by Tobias's creditors, who now work for Harrow. Marisol confronts Tobias; he admits he sold information years ago to survive. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered grudgingly, the family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Night at the Estuary
chapters.summary: Wren and Ezra, alternating POV. They reach the Atlas and find Harrow's men already aboard, searching. A near-catastrophic confrontation ends with Ezra injured and Wren escaping with the ship's register — proof of ownership. Emotional beat: fear hardening into commitment; the Atlas becomes a symbol of shared inheritance.

chapters.title: The Century Turns Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. With December 31st hours away, the household gathers. The trust expires at midnight; whoever presents the letter and signs inherits everything, and the rest may be cast out. Dominic asks Wren to choose fairly. Emotional beat: suffocating weight of a decision designed to divide them.

chapters.title: Each One's Claim
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in turn. Each family member privately tells Wren why they deserve — or refuse — the berth: Marisol for security, Tobias for redemption, Ezra for the sea, Dominic for legacy. Wren realizes the choice is a trap built by lawyers and rivals alike. Emotional beat: heartbreak transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: Harrow Moves at Midnight Eve
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Harrow's men seize the observatory clock tower, intending to destroy the hidden documents at the stroke of midnight and void the trust entirely. Wren understands the master clock itself is the legal witness — its chimes mark the moment of transfer. Emotional beat: race-against-time urgency.

chapters.title: Climbing the Tower
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren climbs through ice and wind to reach the clock room, where Finch, revealed as Harrow's informant-turned-reluctant ally, holds off the men. She reaches the mechanism as the final minutes tick down. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; every skill her family taught her converges.

chapters.title: The Last Chime of 1899
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. At the twelfth chime, Wren stops the clock — freezing the legal moment — then restarts it with a new document inside the case: an amended trust dividing the inheritance equally among all five signatures, witnessed by Finch. Harrow's claim collapses for lack of a sole heir to contest. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; she breaks the game rather than win it.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a New Year
chapters.summary: Tobias, POV. The household reels from victory: lawyers circle, papers are challenged, and Tobias offers to leave to spare them his scandal. Instead, the others present him with his signed share. Emotional beat: belonging affirmed not by worthiness but by insistence.

chapters.title: The Atlas Sails
chapters.summary: Ezra, POV. The refitted Atlas makes her maiden voyage under the household's joint ownership, carrying cargo instead of secrets. Ezra takes the wheel at last. Emotional beat: joy earned slowly; the inheritance becomes a living thing rather than a hoard.

chapters.title: Dominic's Quiet Handover
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Dominic formally retires, giving Wren the workshop keys and admitting he chose her first, years ago, because she measured the world in what could be carried — and stayed anyway. Emotional beat: tender passing of the torch between parent and child of circumstance.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren repairs the observatory clock properly, leaving her own maker's mark beside Finch's and Dominic's old ones. She packs light for a visit to the Atlas, taking only tools and letters. Emotional beat: peace; she has learned that home is not carried but built.

chapters.title: The Brightwater Register
chapters.summary: Full household, POV rotating in a closing chorus. On the first anniversary, the family opens a new register — not of inheritance but of membership — and adds their names alongside those yet to come: another orphan at the door, another stray. Emotional beat: warm resolution; found family endures because someone keeps choosing it, like a clock kept wound.
